parts.visual:
A founder sells their company for $20 Million. They take $1 Million and write ten $100,000 checks to young, hungry founders who are just starting out. Nine of those startups go completely bankrupt. The tenth becomes a $10 Billion unicorn, returning $20 Million to the angel.

The New Role:
1. Angel Investor: A wealthy individual who provides capital for a business start-up, usually in exchange for convertible debt or ownership equity.
2. The Value Add: Unlike giant VC funds that just provide cash, former-founder Angels provide extreme empathy, tactical advice, and introductions, because they have literally fought the exact same battles.
parts.audio: Angel investing is not a way to make safe money. It is a highly expensive hobby that occasionally produces a lottery ticket. Exited founders become Angels to stay connected to the game, without having to work 90 hours a week.

questions.question: A new Angel Investor puts 100% of their investment budget into a single 'brilliant' AI startup. What is the fundamental error?
options: Lack of Portfolio Theory. Seed-stage investing is pure chaos; 90% of companies die regardless of how brilliant the idea is. Angels MUST diversify, writing 20 to 30 smaller checks, knowing that only one 'Power Law' winner will pay for all the losers.
questions.correct_answer: Lack of Portfolio Theory. Seed-stage investing is pure chaos; 90% of companies die regardless of how brilliant the idea is. Angels MUST diversify, writing 20 to 30 smaller checks, knowing that only one 'Power Law' winner will pay for all the losers.
questions.explanation: You cannot pick winners. You can only buy enough tickets to catch the winner.

questions.question: Listen to the experienced Angel Investor explaining their strategy. What do they evaluate most?
questions.tts_text: I don't even read the financial projections in the pitch deck. At the Seed stage, the product will pivot three times anyway. I spend the entire meeting trying to figure out if the founder is resilient enough to survive five years of pure agony.
options: Investing in the Human. At the earliest stages, the business model is a guess. The only permanent asset is the founder's grit, adaptability, and execution speed. You are underwriting the psychology of the team, not the spreadsheet.
questions.correct_answer: Investing in the Human. At the earliest stages, the business model is a guess. The only permanent asset is the founder's grit, adaptability, and execution speed. You are underwriting the psychology of the team, not the spreadsheet.
questions.explanation: A great founder will fix a bad idea. A bad founder will destroy a great idea.

questions.question: What is the danger of a 'Meddling Angel'?
options: An exited founder who writes a $50k check and then demands to act like the CEO, calling the new founders every day to micromanage their product. Good angels give advice when asked, but remember they are no longer driving the car.
questions.correct_answer: An exited founder who writes a $50k check and then demands to act like the CEO, calling the new founders every day to micromanage their product. Good angels give advice when asked, but remember they are no longer driving the car.
questions.explanation: You bought a ticket to the game, but you are not on the field.

questions.question: What is a 'Syndicate' (like on AngelList)?
options: A structure where one famous 'Lead Angel' finds a great startup, and allows hundreds of smaller investors to pool their money together (e.g., $1,000 each) to write one massive check. It democratizes access to elite startup deals.
questions.correct_answer: A structure where one famous 'Lead Angel' finds a great startup, and allows hundreds of smaller investors to pool their money together (e.g., $1,000 each) to write one massive check. It democratizes access to elite startup deals.
questions.explanation: Syndicates give retail investors access to Silicon Valley.
